newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Vintage advises not to sell.
newsitem.headline: Australian Vintage advises not to sell.

text.p: Takeover target Australian Vintage Ltd on Wednesday advised shareholders not to sell their shares to fellow winemaker Simeon Wines Ltd ahead of the completion of an independent expert's report.
Simeon Wines said on Tuesday it intended to seek a merger with Austvin by means of a share and cash offer, valuing the group at about A$111 million.
Simeon said it would offer four of its shares plus A$3.60 cash for every five Austvin shares.
Based on Simeon's A$2.86 closing price on Tuesday, this equates to about A$3.01 per Austvin share.
Austvin last traded on Monday at a 12-month high of A$2.85, before it was suspended on Tuesday at its own request.
Austvin directors said in a statement they would obtain an independent expert's opinion of the offer.

"Australian Vintage directors consider that Simeon is a well run company with attractive assets and good standing in the Australian wine industry and recognise that there may well be strategic value created through an effective merging of both companies," Austvin said in a statement.
"However, directors will rely upon the results of the independent evaluation to formulate a recommendation to shareholders."
It was intended to appoint Ord Minnett Corprate Finance Ltd as corporate advisers and Price Waterhouse Corporate Finance to prepare an independent director's report.
Simeon said on Tuesday a succesful merger would create Australia's fourth largest winemaker by volume.
